_readme: Canonical component-version registry for the self-improving eval/smoke/checkpoint stack.
Any change to a file under a component's `paths` must touch that component's entry in the
same change: bump `version` (new history entry, newest first) or append a same-version
history entry whose note starts with 'no-bump:' explaining why the change is behavior-neutral.
`paths` are repo-relative; a trailing '/' claims a directory prefix; longest prefix wins.
Staleness ordering is the position in `history` (newest first), never string comparison.
New ids and future bumps use monotonic v1, v2, ...; pre-existing native encodings are kept.

Keep repair acceptance below the module ratchet and make synthetic source-verifier fixtures match canonical Git, environment, and runtime identity behavior.
Initialize private Git history in synthetic source-gate fixtures so acceptance tests exercise the same Git-backed source identity as production.
Split oversized recovery and contract-test modules, and simplify runner return paths without relaxing gates.
Declare the intentionally imported cross-module pytest fixture so Ruff and pytest both recognize its use.
Require pytest-collected repair regressions and exercise fail-closed runtime selection.
Make the outer Bubblewrap mounts the trusted repair boundary; require exact pytest regression paths and collected test functions; fail closed on unapproved verifier runtimes.
Require every newly added repair regression to fail on the baseline overlay and pass on the candidate; preserve the original failure and verifier budgets.

Make controller-owned repair version reconciliation atomic and interruption-safe, require authenticated overlay provenance, support every live registry version shape, forbid worker grants for the registry, and let immutable retained proposals complete verification after coding authority expires.

Apply version governance after an isolated repair worker exits: deterministically bump every watched component touched by the worker patch, preserve the worker proposal in the authenticated journal, bind verification and publication to the governed candidate, and independently reject any altered registry overlay.

Exclude the controller-owned execution-release marker from only synthetic private Git indexes, force changed paths through literal pathspecs, prove coverage from frozen verifier snapshots, and remove unpublished stage trees on success, failure, or interruption.

Preserve ignore semantics in controller-owned private Git verification repositories: stage ordinary source with normal Git rules, then force-add only independently verified changed paths so granted ignored regressions remain covered without tracking runtime caches.

Stage an immutable stdlib-only proposal digest command from the trusted controller. It binds the pinned baseline and exact repair grant, hashes granted files through stable no-follow descriptors, and remains advisory to independent full-tree acceptance.

Validate pinned source before owner-write preparation of exact private regular files. Stage the trusted prepared manifest for native namespace projection; retain full physical candidate and scope verification. Source-test coverage exempts only unchanged regular-file owner-write additions that Git cannot represent, while changed bytes, executable bits and types still require coverage.

Expose the digest-bound complete independent verification recipe to Codex, include full repair policies only once, direct structured input reading, reserve termination and scope-validation time inside the repair deadline, and preserve truthful interrupted diagnostics without accepting partial work. Mandatory-isolation mode probes real nested namespaces instead of treating the requirement flag as a prohibition.

Make native Codex tool execution compatible with the outer scoped Bubblewrap sandbox using a temporary empty read-only Git mount target; retain isolated execution receipts and propagate approved runtimes for reproducer verification. No host Git metadata or credentials are mounted.
Reuse explicitly granted host Codex subscription through the existing isolated bridge; activate only independently reconciled delivered source without refilling the original grant.
Bind accepted repair source delivery to controller artifacts and predecessor provenance, preserving scoped authority and original operation identity.
Wire controller-granted provider routes into the isolated repair executor through a fixed-destination Unix bridge with host-only credentials and bounded lifecycle.
Connect ordinary supervised repair to isolated proposals, shared attempt budgets, independent acceptance and source activation.

PLAYBOOK_FAULTS makes the playbook boundary total: discovery import, matches, plan, execute and plan execution now degrade SystemExit to a receipt (step_failed / not-matched) instead of unwinding into the driver. A playbook driving an argparse-based module in process raises SystemExit(2) on a bad argv, so the documented 'a crashing playbook yields a step_failed receipt, never an exception' invariant was false at the seam it was written for. KeyboardInterrupt stays uncaught: the run cap interrupts with SIGINT and kill is not evidence.

run_playbooks prefers a playbook in-process execute (harness_crash -> attempted, data_rebuild -> count-postcondition healed) over the subprocess plan/verify path; same attempt budget, single persisted receipt; execute crash records step_failed.
Merge of cards P10 (heal executors) and P6 (fail-closed heal verification) which both prepended v3 independently; reconciles the component to v4.

harness_crash playbook (class code): captures the failing arm's exit, stderr tail and traceback, names module + harness_family, emits a typed repair_harness action, runs the module's mirrored test file once, and writes an attempted (never healed) receipt. data_rebuild playbook (class data): invokes the driver's rebuild seam under a records_after > records_before postcondition (healed / postcondition_failed). classify routes harness_failure:*:experiment_failed with a non-124 exit to code and rebuild_data prerequisites to data; HealOutcome gains attempted and postcondition_failed.

Driver heal verification primitives (P6): HealVerifyV1-backed record_count_probe + verify_driver_heal write healed / verify_failed (heal_postcondition_failed) receipts and observe the blocker in the escalation ledger; allocate_screening_suite_id scans every _v* of the n family; run_playbooks leaves an 'unhandled' receipt (new HealOutcome) for no_matching_playbook / playbook_declined so escalations are never vacuous.
Fail-closed loop primitives: typed pass outcomes, watchdog blocker catalog, WIP leases, and per-metric power evidence helpers.
